extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry and specialists studying Mochizuki's IUT/abc-related work
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and formal statements used to formulate, compare, and (attempt to) prove the abc-conjecture, Vojta-type height inequalities, Szpiro conjectures, and related constructions (log-diff, log-con, Tate divisors, arithmeticoids) in the context of Mochizuki-style methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholze–Stix core objections (summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Seven core objections of Scholze and Stix (2018) to Mochizuki’s IUT work, listed as (1)–(7) in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the specific mathematical complaints that any verification or rebuttal of Mochizuki must address: (1) lack of demonstration of (distinct) Arithmetic Holomorphic Structures (disambiguation problem); (2) inadequately demonstrated existence/non-triviality of valuation-scaling property of the Θgau-Link; (3) claim that the log-Link is essentially irrelevant; (4) claim that Mochizuki’s Three Indeterminacies must be irrelevant; (5) assertion that the variation in arithmetic (encapsulated by items (1)–(4)) of the hyperplane given by the global product formula is impossible; (6) inference that (2)–(4) give the core conclusion in their Section 2.2; (7) omission of the geometric case. A correct mathematical defense must demonstrate existence/non-triviality and relevance where Scholze–Stix assert absence/irrelevance, or show why those objections do not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of distinct Arithmetic Holomorphic Structures
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim (Scholze–Stix objection (1)) that the existence of (distinct) Arithmetic Holomorphic Structures is not demonstrated in Mochizuki's papers and cannot exist because of a theorem of Mochizuki (2015, Theorem 1.9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any correct account must either construct such distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures or explain and justify the definitions and constructions that show they exist (the author cites [Joshi, 2024c, Theorem 10.11.5.1] and related results as providing existence). This is a central existence/constructibility standard for IUT-style frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-triviality of valuation-scaling property of the Θgau-Link
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholze–Stix objection (2): they assert the existence and non-triviality of the valuation scaling property of the Θgau-Link is not adequately demonstrated and argue it cannot be non-trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valid proof must exhibit or rigorously justify the valuation-scaling (j^2-scaling) factor and any accompanying Galois action that makes Θgau-Link non-trivial. The author references constructions ([Joshi, 2024c]) showing a non-trivial j^2-scaling factor and Galois action as required to refute the objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance of the log‑Link
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholze–Stix objection (3): assertion that the log-Link is essentially irrelevant in Mochizuki's work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A defense must explain how log-Links function as 'proxy for global Frobenius' and how they modify the logarithmic height function (e.g., 'log-Link shaves off multiples of π from the logarithmic height function'), thereby establishing mathematical relevance rather than irrelevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irrelevance of Mochizuki’s Three Indeterminacies
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholze–Stix objection (4): claim that Mochizuki's Three Indeterminacies must be irrelevant to the arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A response must show how the Three Indeterminacies are used or why they are not harmless: either demonstrate that they are meaningful and controlled within the framework or provide constructions/arguments that remove the alleged ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impossibility of arithmetic variation via the global product formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholze–Stix objection (5): assertion of impossibility of the existence of the variation in arithmetic (captured by items (1)–(4)) of the hyperplane given by the global product formula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To rebut this, one must produce constructions or demonstrate mechanisms (e.g., arithmeticoids, log-Links, holomorphoids) that realize the claimed variations compatibly with the global product formula; the author claims such constructions exist in his series of papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrable disproofs of Scholze–Stix assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: The meta-criterion: every impossibility/assertion of Scholze–Stix must be checked against explicit constructions or theorems; the author asserts that each impossibility in Scholze–Stix is invalidated by his work (see Table 1.9.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard for acceptance is explicit mathematical references or theorems that either construct the criticized objects/structures or rigorously show the claimed impossibility is false.

rubrics_metrics.name: abc-conjecture (Conjecture 2.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each ε > 0, there exists C(ε) > 0 such that for all primitive integer triples a + b = c one has max(|a|,|b|,|c|) ≤ C(ε)·(rad(abc))^{1+ε}, where rad(abc)=∏_{p|abc} p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central conjectural inequality to be proven/derived; any claimed proof must show the existence of the function C(ε) and derive the stated inequality for all primitive triples. Remarks note that the exponent is optimal (Stewart–Tijdeman examples) and cannot be weakened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic Szpiro Conjecture (Conjecture 2.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For elliptic curves E/Q, for each ε > 0 there exists C(ε) > 0 such that |Δ_E|_R ≪ C(ε)·N_E^{6+ε}, where Δ_E is the discriminant, N_E the conductor, and |Δ_E|_R denotes appropriate normalized absolute value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The conjecture relates discriminant and conductor exponents for elliptic curves over Q; known geometric analogues and optimality remarks (exponent cannot be lowered) must be taken into account. Proof strategies often relate this conjecture to abc and Vojta-type inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions of bounded discrepancy class
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition: f and g on a set X have the same bounded discrepancy class (f ≈ g) if f(x) = g(x) + O(1) on X; define f . g if f(x) ≤ g(x) + C for some C, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This equivalence-of-functions notion is used throughout comparisons of arithmetic functions (e.g., heights, log-diff, log-con); the definition must be applied carefully (the text warns of a misprint in Mochizuki's earlier definition).

rubrics_metrics.name: log-diff and log-con (definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For X a geometrically connected smooth projective variety over a number field L and D an effective divisor: log-diff_X(P) = (1/[L(P):L])·deg(d_{L(P)/L}) (the normalized arithmetic degree of the different), and log-con_D(P) = (1/[L(P):L])·deg((ι_P(D))_red) (the normalized arithmetic degree of the reduced pullback of D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These two functions depend on (X,D) and the point P; the paper studies their bounded discrepancy class and uses them in height inequalities (noting dependence on minimal field of definition and arithmetic degrees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vojta's Height Inequality for curves (Mochizuki's formulation, Conjecture 2.5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (X,D)/L be a geometrically connected, smooth projective curve and U = X − D hyperbolic; for integer d ≥ 1 and every ε > 0 the inequality ht_{ω_X(D)}(P) ≳ (1+ε)(log-diff_X(P) + log-con_D(P)) holds for P ∈ U( Q̄ ) of degree ≤ d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a central height inequality whose validity for curves implies (and is implied by, in various formulations) abc-type statements; any proof needs to handle normalization, degree-bounded subsets, and the dependence on ε and d.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong abc-conjecture (Mochizuki's formulation, Conjecture 2.6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialized strong form of abc: for (X,D)=(P^1, {0,1,∞}) and for each ε>0, there exists C(ε) such that ht_{ω_{P^1}(D)}(P) ≳ (1+ε)(log-diff + log-con) on suitable bounded sets of degree ≤ d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The strong abc formulation is presented as a Vojta-type inequality on P^1 with punctures and is used to deduce the standard abc by specializing parameters (Proposition 2.6.2 shows strong abc implies abc).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence: strong abc ⇔ Vojta's Height Inequality (van Frankenhuysen, Theorem 2.7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem: The strong abc-conjecture and Vojta's Height Inequality for curves are equivalent (as stated, these two conjectures are equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This equivalence is an important logical relation: proving one gives the other. The result is used to translate between different conjectural frameworks and justifies reductions and reformulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mochizuki's refinement for compactly bounded subsets (Theorem 2.8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For S a finite set of primes and integer d≥1, Vojta’s Height Inequality holds iff Conjecture 2.6.1 holds for any S-supported compactly bounded subset of the relevant degree-bounded set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This refines van Frankenhuysen by showing that proving strong abc on S-supported compactly bounded subsets suffices for the general Vojta inequality. Practical proofs may therefore focus on such compactly bounded subsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main Theorem (Theorem 2.10.1): Vojta holds ⇒ abc, Szpiro, Mordell
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement: For (X,D)/L a geometrically connected smooth projective curve and integer d≥1, for every ε>0 Vojta’s Height Inequality holds on U( Q̄ )≤d; consequently the strong abc (and abc), the Arithmetic Szpiro inequality for elliptic curves over number fields, and an effective form of Mordell's Conjecture follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claimed proof of this main theorem must establish Vojta's inequality in the stated generality (for all such curves and degree bounds) and then deduce the listed consequences via standard implications (citations: Elkies, van Frankenhuysen, etc.). The proof strategy mentioned is to prove the Szpiro-type inequality for suitable compactly bounded subsets and average over arithmetic holomorphic structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminants, differents, Swan conductors as measures of additive structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 3.3.1 and surrounding text: discriminants, differents, and Swan conductors depend on the additive structure of an arithmeticoid and thus measure relative differences between additive structures of two arithmeticoids (distinct arithmetic avatars) of a number field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The criterion is that these classical arithmetic invariants vary with the choice of additive structure (arithmeticoid) and therefore can be used to quantify differences when averaging over arithmetic Teichmüller spaces. The text warns these are not practically useful for explicit computation but are conceptually crucial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and invariance of the Tate divisor and reduced Tate divisor
rubrics_metrics.description: For an elliptic curve C over M, the Tate divisor q_M = Σ_{w∈V_odd,ss} ord_w(q_w)·w (and its reduction f_M = (q_M)^red) is defined via local Tate parameters q_w; the normalized arithmetic degree log(q_M) = deg(q_M)/[M:Q].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A crucial property (Proposition 4.4.4) is that log(q_M) is invariant across finite extensions: if M ⊇ L_mod then log(q_M) = log(q_{L_mod}). This invariance is employed when averaging Tate divisors across arithmeticoids and is necessary for consistency of adelic/idele constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idelic Tate idele → arithmetic divisor correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an idele TI_C/arith(L) = (q_v)_v with q_v a chosen Tate parameter at v, Divisor(TI) = Σ_v ord_v(q_v)·v equals the Tate divisor q_{C/arith(L)}; different choices of local parameters give the same arithmetic divisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identification allows passing between idelic data and arithmetic divisors and is the basis for constructing cohomology classes (via L_v^∗ and its p-adic completions) used in averaging over arithmeticoids and working in Galois cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer and Galois-cohomological identification of idelic factors (4.5.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification L_v^* (p-adic completion limit) ≃ H^1(G_{L_v}, Q_p(1)) via Kummer theory, enabling an idele of Tate parameters to be viewed as a compatible system of Galois cohomology classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the technical bridge used to 'collate' Tate idele classes arising from many distinct arithmeticoids into a subset of H^1(arith(L)_y, Q(1)); any averaging/volume computation in the proof must respect this cohomological identification and compatibility conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Averaging/collation principle for Tate idele cohomology classes (Proposition 4.5.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a collection A of arithmeticoids and chosen Tate idele cohomology classes TI_{C/arith(L)_z} for each, there exists a subset Ψ_{C,A} inside H^1(arith(L)_y0, Q(1)) consisting of the images (under factorwise topological isomorphisms) of the union of the images of those TI classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proposition formalizes how Tate idele cohomology classes from many arithmetic holomorphic structures can be embedded/collated into the cohomology of a fixed standard arithmeticoid—an essential step for the averaging arguments used in the paper (and in Mochizuki's methods). The proposition requires careful choice of topological isomorphisms and compatibility data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of normalized arithmetic degree of different and discriminant (Proposition 4.3.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite extension M/Q, log d_M (normalized arithmetic degree of the different) equals log disc_{M/Q} (normalized arithmetic degree of the field discriminant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identity is standard (cited to Bombieri–Gubler) and must be used consistently when relating differents to discriminants in averaging and height comparisons; proofs relying on differents may equivalently use discriminants via this equality.
